newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey plans state sector debt write-off.
newsitem.headline: Turkey plans state sector debt write-off.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist-conservative coalition government is planning to launch a new plan to allow public sector institutions to write off debts with each other, Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Thursday.

"Our government will enable public institutions to set off their debts to each other...Therefore they will get rid of their heavy interest burden," Erbankan told reporters before a cabinet meeting. He did not give any further details.
But Ufuk Soylemez, state minister in charge of the treasury, told reporters in Istanbul he was unaware of the plan.
"I have no information about the issue," Soylemez, a minister from the coalition's centre-right wing, said shortly after Erbakan made his remarks.
Economists said Erbakan's plan would not bring any benefit to the economy, but would increase the debt burden of the cash-short treasury.
"In all earlier debt write-offs, the treasury undertook the net balance of receivables. It will be the same if they go for the plan," said a senior government economist.

Economists, declining to be named, said implementation of such a plan would weaken fiscal discipline in the public sector and encourage state institutions to borrow in anticipation that another write-off plan would erase their debts.

The latest public sector debt write-off in 1992 failed to solve Turkey's mounting fiscal problems. The country is still struggling with a huge public sector deficit expected to exceed 10 percent of gross domestic product in 1996.
Bankers say the plan, which they believe was prepared by the coalition's Islamist wing, Erbakan's Welfare Party, is expected to face opposition from the centre-right wing of the ruling alliance.
